news.headline: Robinhood Misses Q1 Revenue & EBITDA Estimates; HOOD Falls ~9% After Hours
news.body: Robinhood reported Q1 2026 revenue of $1.07 billion (vs. $1.13–1.18 billion estimated) and EPS of $0.38 (vs. ~$0.42–0.44 consensus), with adjusted EBITDA of $534 million missing the $582 million forecast by 8.2%. Crypto trading revenue collapsed 47% year-over-year as the digital asset market slumped, the dominant driver of the miss despite 15% overall revenue growth. HOOD stock fell ~9% in after-hours trading; the company provided no 2026 revenue guidance and disclosed an additional $100 million investment to support the Treasury's Trump Accounts program. The miss highlights Robinhood's continued vulnerability to crypto market cycles as it works to diversify into wealth management, banking, and prediction markets.

news.headline: WSJ Report: OpenAI Missed Revenue & User Targets, Dragging AI Stocks Lower
news.body: A Wall Street Journal report published April 28 revealed OpenAI missed multiple monthly revenue targets in early 2026 and fell short of a goal to reach 1 billion weekly ChatGPT users, with CFO Sarah Friar privately warning the company may struggle to fund its massive data-center commitments if growth doesn't accelerate. Oracle, which holds a $300 billion five-year compute deal with OpenAI, dropped over 4%; CoreWeave fell ~6%; Broadcom and AMD each shed ~4%; Nvidia declined ~3%. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.9% and the Nasdaq-100 dropped 1.5% on the day, as investors re-examined the sustainability of AI capex across the sector. OpenAI pushed back, calling the report 'clickbait' and saying the business was 'firing on all cylinders.'

news.headline: Spotify Slides 12% on Weak Q2 Profit Guidance Despite Q1 User Beat
news.body: Spotify reported Q1 2026 EPS of $3.46, beating estimates of $3.03, but revenue of $4.54 billion missed the $4.62 billion consensus, with ad-supported revenue declining 5% year-over-year for a second consecutive quarter. The stock tumbled over 12% as Q2 operating income guidance came in below analyst expectations, spooking investors despite monthly active users rising 12% YoY to 761 million and premium subscribers climbing 9% to 293 million. Management framed the ad weakness as a near-term hurdle and pointed to AI-driven personalization tools in beta, but the soft forward guidance overshadowed the subscriber momentum. Markets care because the miss signals continued monetization challenges in digital audio and raises questions about ARPU expansion from recent price hikes.

news.headline: General Motors Crushes Q1 Estimates; EPS $3.70 vs. $2.62 Expected, Raises Guidance
news.body: General Motors reported Q1 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.70, trouncing the LSEG consensus of $2.62, as the automaker posted $4.2 billion in adjusted earnings versus the ~$3 billion expected. GM raised its full-year 2026 EBITDA outlook to $13.5–$15.5 billion, up $500 million from prior guidance, and lifted full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $11.50–$13.50. Shares traded more than 4% higher on the day, signaling the market's relief that GM is holding up despite high gas prices and geopolitical uncertainty. The beat reinforces that domestic vehicle demand and pricing power remain resilient heading into the key summer selling season.

news.headline: Coca-Cola Jumps 6% After Best Organic Growth in Five Quarters, Lifts Full-Year EPS Guide
news.body: Coca-Cola posted Q1 2026 revenue of $12.47 billion (vs. $12.24 billion expected) and adjusted EPS of $0.86 (vs. $0.81 consensus), with organic revenue growth of 10%—the company's strongest in five quarters—driven by a 13% volume surge in Coke Zero Sugar and global unit case volume up 3% versus the 1% analyst expectation. The company raised its full-year comparable EPS growth outlook to 8–9% from 7–8% and reiterated its 4–5% organic revenue growth target. Shares surged ~6% to above $80, the best single-day performance in years, benefiting from a defensive rotation as tech stocks sold off on the OpenAI report. The results underscore Coca-Cola's pricing power and brand resilience even as some consumer segments face pressure from inflation and Middle East conflict uncertainty.

news.headline: Lightelligence Surges 383% on HK Debut in Largest Main Board IPO Pop in a Decade
news.body: Shanghai Xizhi Technology (Lightelligence), China's first publicly listed AI photonics chipmaker, surged 383.6% on its Hong Kong main board debut on April 28, closing at HK$886 against an IPO price of HK$183.20 — the largest first-day gain for a main board listing in nearly 10 years. The IPO raised HK$2.4 billion, with the retail tranche oversubscribed 5,785 times; cornerstone investors included Alibaba, GIC, Temasek, BlackRock, and Fidelity. The company, which leads China's third-party scale-up optical interconnect market, remains loss-making with a 1.3 billion yuan net loss in 2025 on 106 million yuan revenue, highlighting the speculative premium markets are placing on AI infrastructure plays. The listing sets the first public benchmark for optical computing as an asset class and is expected to accelerate follow-on AI semiconductor offerings on HKEX.

news.headline: SoftBank Tumbles ~10% on Tokyo as OpenAI Misses Revenue and User Growth Targets
news.body: SoftBank Group (9984.T) fell 9.86% to ¥5,268 on April 28 — its steepest single-session drop in six months and the worst performer on the Nikkei 225 — after the Wall Street Journal reported OpenAI missed internal user and revenue growth projections, sparking concern over the sustainability of SoftBank's $30 billion follow-on investment commitment. SoftBank holds an approximately 11% stake in OpenAI and has already deployed the first $10 billion tranche via a bridge facility, with two further $10 billion installments scheduled for July and October. The sell-off dragged broader Asian tech sentiment, with Hitachi down 5.8% and Tokyo Electron off 4.1% on the same session. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman disputed the report, but the market reaction underscored how deeply SoftBank's valuation is now tethered to OpenAI's growth narrative.

news.headline: Korea Stock Market Overtakes UK to Rank 8th Globally on AI Chip Surge
news.body: South Korea's total stock market capitalisation surged over 45% this year to $4.04 trillion, surpassing the UK's $4.04 trillion and vaulting the KOSPI to 8th place among global bourses, Bloomberg data confirmed on April 28. The KOSPI broke intraday through the 6,700 mark for the first time before closing at 6,641, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix — whose combined record Q1 earnings underpinned the rally — now accounting for more than 40% of total market cap. The UK market was roughly double Korea's size as recently as end-2024, making the reversal one of the fastest in modern market history. Goldman Sachs raised its KOSPI target to 8,000, citing a 200%-plus upward revision to its 2026 earnings growth forecast driven by AI chip demand.

news.headline: CATL Prices $5B HK Share Placement at Low End; Stock Falls Up to 9.2% on Dilution
news.body: Contemporary Amperex Technology (3750.HK) raised HK$39.2 billion (~$5 billion) in Hong Kong's largest share placement of 2026, pricing at HK$628.20 per share — the bottom of the HK$628.20–HK$651.80 range and a 7% discount to the prior close. More than 150 entities participated, including hedge funds, sovereign wealth funds, and existing shareholders, but shares fell as much as 9.2% intraday to HK$613.50 on April 28 as dilution concerns outweighed deal demand. Net proceeds are earmarked for global new-energy projects, R&D, and overseas expansion as CATL accelerates its zero-carbon strategy amid the Iran-driven oil shock tailwind for EV adoption. HSBC maintained a Buy with a raised HK$790 price target, citing CATL's Q1 net profit of 20.7 billion yuan, up 49% year-on-year.

news.headline: Nikkei Hits All-Time High Above 60,500; KOSPI Scales Fresh Record at 6,615 on Semis
news.body: Japan's Nikkei 225 closed at a record 60,537.36 on April 27, up 1.38%, crossing the 60,000 milestone for the first time as semiconductor and AI-linked stocks surged on strong earnings momentum and continued foreign inflows tied to Japan's governance reform rally. South Korea's KOSPI simultaneously jumped 2.15% to a fresh all-time high of 6,615.03, powered by semiconductor heavyweights led by SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics on robust memory and HBM demand for AI data centers. China's CSI 300 was little changed after March industrial profits accelerated to +15.8% year-on-year, beating the prior month's +15.2%. Both Japan and Korea's record highs were achieved against a backdrop of stalled U.S.–Iran negotiations, demonstrating Asia's tech-led equity resilience to ongoing geopolitical risks.

news.headline: UAE Quits OPEC and OPEC+ Effective May 1, Ending 59-Year Membership
news.body: The United Arab Emirates announced on April 28 it will leave OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, ending nearly six decades of membership, citing national interest and a desire to pursue an independent output strategy. The UAE was OPEC's third-largest producer before the Iran war, accounting for roughly 12% of the cartel's supply, with capacity of approximately 4.8 million barrels per day. Near-term market impact is muted because the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed and UAE exports are bottlenecked regardless of quota status; however, analysts warn the exit could trigger contagion, with Kazakhstan flagged as a potential next departure. Post-conflict, the UAE's freedom to ramp output uncapped could flood markets and structurally undermine OPEC's price-management role.

news.headline: WTI Surges ~4% Past $100/bbl as Trump Rejects Iran Hormuz Proposal
news.body: WTI crude futures climbed nearly 4% to above $100 per barrel on April 28, extending a seventh consecutive session of gains and hitting their highest level since early April, after President Trump was reported dissatisfied with Iran's latest Strait of Hormuz reopening proposal. Iran conveyed via Pakistani mediators that it would cease hostilities if the US lifted its naval blockade and deferred nuclear talks, but Washington rejected the terms with Tehran's nuclear program remaining the central sticking point. Brent touched $111.57/bbl, with Hormuz loadings running at just 3.8 million bpd — down from over 20 million pre-conflict — keeping the supply shock at historically unprecedented scale per the IEA. Markets now await the May 3 OPEC+ meeting and any counteroffer from Washington, with the IEA warning of a potential demand slowdown compounding the supply crisis.

news.headline: Saudi Arabia Eyes $5–$12/bbl Cut to June Asia OSPs as War Rally Fades
news.body: Saudi Arabia is expected to slash its official selling prices for June-loading crude to Asia by $5 to $12 per barrel from record highs set for May, according to a Reuters survey of Asian refinery sources published April 28. Arab Light's June OSP could fall to a premium of $7.50–$14.50/bbl over Dubai/Oman, down from a record $19.50 premium for May, as Asian spot market premiums softened sharply and Chinese refiners cut May Saudi crude purchases to a record low of 20 million barrels due to margin pressure. Replacement cargoes from the US, West Africa, and Russian crude under US waivers are filling part of the gap, easing the acute panic-buying premium. The wide forecast range signals ongoing uncertainty and the potential for a significant realignment of crude pricing dynamics once Hormuz eventually reopens.

news.headline: Asia LNG Imports Hit 7-Year Low in March; Qatar Infrastructure Damage Delays Supply Wave
news.body: Asian LNG imports fell 4.3% year-on-year to 21.12 million tonnes in March 2026, the lowest March figure in seven years, as the Strait of Hormuz closure stranded all Qatari and UAE supply, per the Gas Exporting Countries Forum. The IEA separately warned that damage to Qatar's Ras Laffan liquefaction facility — the world's largest, offline since a March 2 attack — will delay the anticipated global LNG supply expansion wave by at least two years, with a cumulative supply loss of ~120 billion cubic metres projected between 2026 and 2030. Asian LNG spot prices surged over 140% following QatarEnergy's force majeure declaration, squeezing South Asian buyers particularly hard; China's 30-day rolling LNG import average in April hit its lowest level since 2018. The medium-term supply tightness now extends well beyond the conflict itself, fundamentally repricing LNG market risk for the rest of the decade.

news.headline: Gold Falls ~2% to 3-Week Low as BOJ Turns Hawkish and Oil Inflation Fears Mount
news.body: Spot gold dropped approximately 1.8–2% to around $4,578–$4,615/oz on April 28, its lowest level since early April, as surging oil prices intensified inflation fears and the Bank of Japan's hawkish tilt — keeping rates on hold but significantly raising its fiscal 2026 inflation forecast with three board members proposing hikes — amplified rate-sensitive pressure on non-yielding bullion. Silver fell a sharper 3.54% to $73.22/oz, reflecting its higher beta in risk-off sessions, while the 10-year US Treasury yield climbed to a 3-week high. Markets are now pricing a hawkish hold from the Fed at its April 29–30 meeting, with Julius Baer analyst Carsten Menke noting that gold's decline directly mirrors the rise in oil driven by stalled US–Iran talks. A Reuters poll of 31 analysts published April 27 nonetheless raised the median 2026 gold price forecast to a record $4,916/oz, suggesting the selloff is viewed by institutions as a buying opportunity rather than a structural break.
